sources.title: Empowering innovation: The next generation of the Phi family
sources.evidence: Dated February 26, 2025, announces Phi-4-mini as newly available in the Phi family. Describes a nominal 3.8B dense decoder-only Transformer with grouped-query attention, shared embeddings and function calling. The prose describes sequences up to 128,000 tokens.

sources.title: Phi-4-mini-instruct official model card
sources.evidence: Identifies the released instruction checkpoint, text inputs and outputs, multilingual support, nominal 3.8B parameters, 128K context, supervised fine-tuning and DPO. Documents native function-calling prompts using tool delimiters and JSON tool definitions. Supplies loading instructions for open weights and states MIT licensing.

sources.title: Phi-4-mini-instruct checkpoint configuration
sources.evidence: Specifies 32 layers, hidden size 3072, intermediate size 8192, 24 query and 8 KV heads, vocabulary 200064, tied embeddings, BF16 and no attention/MLP/head biases. max_position_embeddings is 131072. No expert routing or quantization configuration. Reopened October 27, 2026 at the same pinned revision; these configuration, implementation and index facts are unchanged.

sources.title: Phi-4-mini-instruct model implementation
sources.evidence: Defines embedding, bias-free fused QKV/output and gated-MLP projections, two learned RMSNorms per block, final RMSNorm and tied language-model head. Rotary inverse frequencies are nonpersistent buffers. These modules establish which header entries are learned parameters and avoid counting the tied head twice. Reopened October 27, 2026 at the same pinned revision; these configuration, implementation and index facts are unchanged.

sources.title: Phi-4-mini-instruct checkpoint tensor index
sources.evidence: Maps 194 tensor keys to two shards. Every key and shape was reconciled with the implementation and configuration. The 7,672,043,520-byte tensor-data total agrees with the learned-parameter count at BF16; bytes alone were not used to infer the count. Reopened October 27, 2026 at the same pinned revision; these configuration, implementation and index facts are unchanged.

sources.title: Phi-4-mini-instruct first shard header
sources.evidence: Original October 26 audit: Read only the 8-byte length and 13,000-byte JSON header using HTTP 206 ranges. Contains 111 BF16 learned tensors totaling 2,451,812,352 parameters. All shapes match expected architecture tensors; no scales, packed weights or buffers appear. Not downloaded again during the parameter re-audit.

sources.title: Phi-4-mini-instruct second shard header
sources.evidence: Original October 26 audit: Read only the 8-byte length and 9,680-byte JSON header using HTTP 206 ranges. Contains 83 BF16 learned tensors totaling 1,384,209,408 parameters. All shapes match expected architecture tensors; combined shard keys exactly match the index. Not downloaded again during the parameter re-audit.

sources.title: Phi-4-mini-instruct MIT license
sources.evidence: The repository license is the MIT License, copyrighted by Microsoft Corporation; the model card explicitly applies it to the model.

sources.title: Phi-4-Mini Technical Report
sources.evidence: Sections 2 and 2.1 give dense decoder Transformer details: 32 layers, width 3072, tied embeddings, 24 query/8 KV heads and LongRoPE 128K context. The abstract footnote and section 3.1.3 explicitly distinguish the experimental reasoning-enhanced model and say its CoT training data was not applied to the officially released Phi-4-Mini checkpoint.

sources.title: Phi-4-Mini-Reasoning: Exploring the Limits of Small Reasoning Language Models in Math
sources.evidence: Later first-party report identifies Phi-4-Mini as the 3.8B starting model and explains the additional long-CoT training and reinforcement learning that produce the distinct Phi-4-Mini-Reasoning. It does not disclose a separate per-token active count for Phi-4-Mini.

sources.title: Phi-4-mini-instruct repository metadata
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026: current revision remains cfbefacb99257ffa30c83adab238a50856ac3083 and metadata still reports 3,836,021,760 BF16 tensor elements. The original audit reconciled this with the complete learned count using config, code and shard headers; this re-audit rechecked config, code and index without requesting shards. Repository creation was February 19, 2025, distinct from the February 26 public launch.

sources.title: Qwen3 Technical Report, Table 20
sources.evidence: Freshly opened October 27, 2026. Table 20 compares non-reasoning baselines and explicitly lists Phi-4-mini with 3.8B under both Activated Params and Total Params. This supports the Qwen Team's nominal active-count convention for the released instruction model; it is not a Microsoft disclosure or an exact accounting of individual tensors executed per token.

sources.title: Sigma-MoE-Tiny Technical Report, Figure 1
sources.evidence: Freshly opened October 27, 2026. December 19, 2025 report by Microsoft Research. Visually inspected the original overview.svg: Figure 1 names Phi-4-mini-instruct and places it at approximately 3.8B on the Activated Parameters (Billions) axis. This later original research comparison corroborates the nominal scale, but supplies no exact component or per-token participation count. Qwen Table 20 supplies the explicit 3.8B tabular value.

sources.title: Reasoning reimagined: Introducing Phi-4-mini-flash-reasoning
sources.evidence: Freshly opened during the October 27 search for later disclosures. The July 9, 2025 launch describes a separate 3.8B reasoning model with a new SambaY decoder-hybrid-decoder architecture. Its size and architecture do not revise the original Phi-4-mini-instruct checkpoint or establish a new active count for that checkpoint.

name.note: The official launch uses Phi-4-mini; the released weights are Phi-4-mini-instruct. Retain the valid short name while identifying the exact instruction checkpoint; this is not Phi-4-mini-reasoning or Phi-4-mini-flash-reasoning.

developer.note: Microsoft announces and licenses the model.

family.note: Member of Microsoft's Phi family, specifically its Phi-4 generation.

release_date.note: The dated Microsoft announcement states the model is newly available. February 19 repository creation is not evidence of public release; the March 3 technical report is later.

open_weights.note: Publicly accessible original BF16 checkpoint shards and documented local loading establish open weights.

license.note: The official model card applies the repository MIT License to these weights.

parameters_b.note: Retain the previously reconciled exact complete learned count, 3,836,021,760. Freshly reopened pinned config, implementation and tensor index remain consistent with the original 194-tensor audit, and current repository metadata independently repeats the count. Tied embedding/head counted once; nonpersistent RoPE buffers excluded. Microsoft's card and report publish nominal 3.8B. No new shard download or tensor census was performed.

active_parameters_b.note: Qwen Team's original Table 20 explicitly reports 3.8B Activated Params for the Phi-4-mini non-reasoning baseline. Adopt that nominal research comparison convention, not an inference that dense total equals active. The later Microsoft Research Sigma report plots the exact Phi-4-mini-instruct checkpoint at approximately 3.8B active. The original Microsoft card, Mini report and Mini-Reasoning report do not separately define an exact per-token active count; neither comparison establishes exact component participation.

architecture.note: Dense decoder-only Transformer with 32 layers, grouped-query attention and tied input/output embeddings. Phi3ForCausalLM is the implementation class, not a claim that this is a Phi-3 checkpoint. The multimodal sibling's mixture of LoRAs does not apply to this text model.

context_window.note: The exact released checkpoint config sets max_position_embeddings=131072, consistent with the card's 128K. Microsoft launch prose says 128,000; use the machine-readable checkpoint limit for this open-weight record and retain this discrepancy. This does not certify a hosted provider limit.

modalities.note: Text input and generated text output; the independently released Phi-4-multimodal is outside this record.

reasoning.note: False means no dedicated extended-reasoning variant/mode in this checkpoint, not inability to solve reasoning tasks. Microsoft explicitly separates the reasoning-enhanced model and its training from released Phi-4-Mini; the later report names that derivative Phi-4-Mini-Reasoning.

tool_call.note: Native function-calling training and a documented tool-delimited prompt format support tool-call generation.

description.value: Microsoft's multilingual text instruction model, released as Phi-4-mini-instruct, with native function calling.
description.note: Replace the broad low-latency agent-task characterization with directly documented instruction, multilingual and function-calling properties.

patch.description: Microsoft's multilingual text instruction model, released as Phi-4-mini-instruct, with native function calling.
patch.notes: Phi-4-mini is the launch name of Phi-4-mini-instruct. Exact checkpoint count is 3,836,021,760 learned parameters with tied input/output embedding counted once; Microsoft publishes nominal 3.8B. Active 3.8B follows Qwen Team's explicit benchmark convention, corroborated approximately by Microsoft Research's later Sigma comparison; neither is an exact per-token tensor count. Config specifies 131,072 context tokens; launch prose says 128,000 and the card says 128K. The dedicated reasoning model is a separate release.

summary: Parameter re-audit retained exact 3.83602176B total after reopening the unchanged official config, code, index, card and repository metadata. Replaced undisclosed active count with nominal 3.8B from Qwen Team's explicit Table 20, corroborated by Microsoft Research's later Sigma Figure 1 for Phi-4-mini-instruct. Attribution and plot precision are explicit; exact per-token participation remains unspecified. Later Mini-Reasoning and Mini-Flash-Reasoning sources concern distinct models. Preserved all 12 unrelated assessments; no shards downloaded or new tensor census performed.
